subject: Model match proposal and trial scope for Valence AI
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Thompson <claire@valence.ai>, Tom Reyes <tom@valence.ai>
Cc: Valence.ai Procurement <procure@valence.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Model match proposal and trial scope for Valence AI

Hi Claire / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a proposed next step so we can get a focused trial running:

Goal: validate open-model alternatives against your proprietary QA baseline for the customer support routing and summarization flows, with explicit parity gates for precision on intent extraction and summary factuality.

Recommended model candidates to trial (shortlist):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (open) — good instruction-following, low latency for 1–2 token streams.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (open) — strong contextual coherence for threading and summary.
- OpenLM-30B (open, distilled variant) — higher-capacity option for long-form summarization.
- Internal baseline: your current vendor-prop model (you noted ~95% intent precision on in-house tests) — we will use this as the baseline for parity.

Acceptance thresholds (proposal):
- Intent extraction precision >= 0.92 (goal to match baseline within a 3% delta)
- Summary factuality score (annotator A/B) >= 0.88
- Average 95th percentile latency (in our dedicated trial infra) <= 220ms
- Token cost per 1k <= target you set during call (we put a placeholder to finalize when we have tokenization counts)

Data & artifacts we need from you to run a representative benchmark:
1) valence_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompts + expected labels) — we can run deterministic evals + blind human audits.
2) A small holdout of historical transcripts (anonymized) for regression checks.
3) Any guardrail / post-processing logic you run in prod (we'll reproduce it in the runner).

Proposed trial plan (3 weeks):
- Week 0: onboarding, infra access, and confirm data/format.
- Week 1: bulk runs of the three open candidates + baseline; automated metrics.
- Week 2: human annotation for summary factuality + signal analysis.
- End: readout and recommendation + suggested rollout (canary OSS model -> regional rollout).

Attachments: proposal_model_matrix.xlsx (candidate matrix + expected compute/quantization options), benchmark_results_template.csv (format for results).

Ask: Can you share the valence_prompt_set_v1.csv and the procurement contact for a trial MSA? If yes, we will schedule a kickoff this week.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

---

From: Claire Thompson <claire@valence.ai>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Model match proposal and trial scope for Valence AI

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications:

1) Intent precision target: our internal baseline precision is 0.95 on the last 6 months of labeled tickets; we are open to a 3–4% delta during the trial but would need a clear path to match it in the roadmap.
2) For summary factuality: we use a 3-annotator majority vote (binary factual / not-factual) plus a short rubric; we will provide the rubric as part of the prompt set.
3) Trial data: I can share the valence_prompt_set_v1.csv and a small anonymized transcript set by EOD tomorrow. Procurement (procure@valence.ai) is looped for MSA questions — they will review the trial terms and SSO/KMS requirements.

A couple asks from our side: can you include recommended quantization tiers (e.g., 8-bit vs 4-bit) and the expected memory footprint for Llama-2-13B-chat vs Mistral-Instruct-7B in the matrix? Also — please call out any quality regression risk when applying aggressive quantization.

If those items are in the document you attached, send a short note pointing to the rows. Otherwise, if you can send a quick follow-up with those numbers that will speed procurement. We prefer a 3-week pilot window.

Thanks,
Claire Thompson
Head of Product — Valence AI
claire@valence.ai

Attachments: (I'll upload the prompt set and rubric to the Drive link you shared)

Jordan / team —

Attached is a quick one-pager (pasted below) and a schedule for the trial runs. I've also uploaded a micro-benchmark CSV to the Drive folder.

Key quantization notes (short):
- FP16: safe baseline, minimal quality delta, highest memory use.
- 8-bit (GPTQ-style): ~1.8x memory reduction vs FP16; expected small quality delta for intent extraction (<1.5% on our internal probes).
- 4-bit (aggressive, q4_0): significant memory benefit but non-zero risk for summarization factuality; expect occasional hallucination increases — recommend 4-bit only for candidate smoke tests, not final evaluation for factuality gating.

Estimated peak GPU memory (approx):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: FP16 18GB | 8-bit 10GB | 4-bit 6GB
- Llama-2-13B-chat: FP16 36GB | 8-bit 20GB | 4-bit 11GB
- OpenLM-30B (distilled): FP16 60GB | 8-bit 34GB | 4-bit 19GB

95th p95 latency (in ms) on c6-dedicated (batch size 1, typical prompt length):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: 120ms
- Llama-2-13B-chat: 190ms
- OpenLM-30B: 350ms

Plan & next steps:
- Wed morning: run smoke tests (8-bit) against valence_prompt_set_v1.csv.
- Wed afternoon: full FP16 runs for metrics collection + output dump for human annotation.
- Thu: annotation prep and kickoff with Marissa's workflow.

Attachments uploaded: benchmark_results_template.csv (filled partly), schedule_trail_runs.csv.

I'll join the kickoff with Claire on Thursday to walk through risk notes.

-Vivek
